verdicts.quote: One unauthenticated HTTP request of a few dozen bytes makes the server process allocate memory proportional to an integer the attacker chose.
verdicts.why: Same defect by mechanism. N06 is located at openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:953, the loop inside sliceMapToSlice that the advisory identifies, and says the array index taken verbatim from the query parameter name sizes the slice allocation, yielding OOM of the whole process from one tiny unauthenticated request - the advisory's mechanism and impact. It traces the deepObject route (DecodeObject :661-687 -> makeObject :911 -> the array branch) and additionally notes the default form/explode style reaches the same sink, which is extra reach, not a different defect; it also places the allocation ahead of the controls that would stop it (inside request validation, before the handler, before any authorization check, before any per-route quota). The nearest other candidates - N04 (regexp recompiled per query key, CPU only), N05 (YAML alias expansion), N14 (unbounded io.ReadAll of bodies) - are different defects and were not used.
